bunnings-corr-zinc.note: NZD 64.94 per 3 m sheet. GST and effective cover not established in retrieved product text; no tax-inclusive area conversion is published.

bunnings-corr-galv.note: NZD 67.93 per 3 m sheet. Same retailer as the zinc and painted observations, not independent market quotes.

roofcrowd-catalog.note: Custom Orb catalogue range is NZD 16.41 to 26.40 excluding GST. The retrieved catalogue does not establish the charging unit or variant at each endpoint, so this is not treated as a per-metre quote.

kennedys-orb.title: Custom Orb on a Kennedys Bush home
kennedys-orb.note: Publisher-reported project. Corrugated pitched areas and membrane flat areas belong to one home, not one universal roof specification.

st-plumbdek.note: Manufacturer profile identity and published 3° starting pitch. Confirm the current specification for the supplying branch.

st-plumbdek-machine.title: Plumbdek production in Christchurch

dim-veedek.title: Veedek roofing profile
dim-veedek.note: Manufacturer lists 755 mm cover, 810 mm sheet width and a 3° starting minimum. The performance table supports 0.40 and 0.55 mm; an N/A column is not treated as an available thickness.

ri-trimrib.title: Trimrib product family
ri-trimrib.note: Use the named Trimrib family and local variants. Unrelated Eurostyle boilerplate on the page is not evidence that Trimrib is a concealed-fix tray.

ri-trimrib-library.title: Trimrib S, TS and V specification listing
ri-trimrib-library.note: Manufacturer-authored library entry describes the swage variants and a 3° starting minimum. It does not justify assigning one universal cover to every Trimrib variant.

ri-trimrib-details.title: Trimrib CAD and flashing details directory
ri-trimrib-details.note: The directory lists both soft-edge and scribed/notched ridge details. Listing a detail is not approval for every roof; use the matching current drawing and specification.

freeman-five.title: Five Rib roofing profile
freeman-five.note: The stated family varies from 754 to 765 mm cover and 25 to 29 mm rib height. Its own guidance distinguishes the 3° starting minimum from a 10° end-lapped condition.

freeman-six.title: Six Rib roofing profile
freeman-six.note: Six Rib is a separate product geometry. Do not substitute five-rib order dimensions or accessories based only on visual similarity.

trs-five.title: TRS5 longrun profile
trs-five.note: Manufacturer lists a maximum effective cover of 760 mm, 0.40/0.55 mm BMT and a 3° starting minimum. Roof-specific load and drainage conditions remain relevant.

mrm-flashings.title: Code of Practice: flashings
mrm-flashings.note: Sections 8.8.1 and 8.8.2 distinguish soft-edge and notched options. Low trapezoidal profiles are not universally required to use notched flashing. Read the current online Code of Practice; a web summary is not installation design.

mrm-bmt.title: Base metal thickness definition
mrm-bmt.note: BMT refers to metal thickness before coatings. An unexplained merchant gauge is not automatically a BMT specification.

mrm-ponding.title: Code of Practice: ponding
mrm-ponding.note: Drainage and ponding context. A profile label or coating does not replace roof-specific pitch and drainage design.

bunnings-five.title: Armorsteel 830 mm Big 5, 0.4 mm, Thunder Grey
bunnings-five.note: Indexed product text lists $30.35/lm. 830 mm is not accepted as confirmed effective cover. Colour, order length, local availability and current checkout price need confirmation.

bunnings-gst.title: Online and special-order terms
bunnings-gst.note: NZ online and special-order terms establish the GST-inclusive price convention. Terms are evidence of tax basis, not another independent price observation.

mitre-five-colour.title: Roofing Industries roofing iron, colour
mitre-five-colour.note: Indexed product listing gives $31.28/lm and a 0.40 mm Trimrib option. Confirm the actual selected variant and branch; no effective cover is assigned from this listing.

mitre-five-unpainted.title: Roofing Industries roofing iron, unpainted
mitre-five-unpainted.note: Indexed product listing gives $23.38/lm. A malformed width field is excluded, not silently corrected into an effective-cover measurement.

renovation-five.title: New 5 Rib zinc roofing, 3.6 m
renovation-five.note: Indexed listing: $73 per 3.6 m sheet, new Armorsteel Zenium, 0.4 BMT, 760 mm coverage. GST basis was not established. This is new stock as described, not a recycled-sheet benchmark.

cc-warranty.note: Location, environment and maintenance conditions matter. No universal distance-from-the-sea rule or guaranteed service life is inferred.

point-wells-trimrib.note: Contractor-reported project combines a named Trimrib roof with other roof systems and detailed skylight work. No standalone roof price or measured roof area established.

tile-sa-guide.note: General guide includes a material-only category, but not an identifiable pressed-tile SKU or a quoted full-system supply schedule. Kept out of material-rate calculations.

tile-riggall.note: Installer explicitly describes removing metal tiles and fitting new purlins for long-run. Does not establish the nationwide frequency of that choice.

tile-overlay.note: Manufacturer describes a CF Shake overlay option. This is not blanket approval to disturb asbestos or cover a damaged structure.

tile-brookfield.note: Builder-authored project description, not the platform-generated summary. Uses the historical Stratos Smooth product name. The 182 m² figure is house size, not roof area.

tile-telfer.title: Architecturally designed home with CF Shake
tile-telfer.note: Kerikeri new-build gallery linked to Telfer House. Counted as one project, not separate gallery and case-study jobs.

tile-kumeu.title: Transforming Kumeu with Shake
tile-kumeu.note: Manufacturer gallery confirms Kumeu location, Shake and Charcoal. Limited project specification; no roof area or price. Presented as a residential application, not a priced new-build case study.

cp-quotes-2026.title: Quotes and estimates
cp-quotes-2026.note: NZ government consumer guidance reviewed 21 October 2026. Distinguishes quotes from estimates, says accepted fixed quotes can only change where a variation is agreed, and states there is no legal requirement to pay a deposit; if one is requested, its consumer guidance says not to pay more than 10% of total cost.

comcom-quotes-2026.title: Quotes, estimates and invoicing
comcom-quotes-2026.note: NZ Commerce Commission guidance reviewed 20 October 2026. Defines quotes and estimates, requires agreement for extra work outside an accepted quote, and states quotes or estimates should be inclusive of GST.

ird-gst-2026.title: What GST is
ird-gst-2026.note: Inland Revenue page last updated 1 April 2026. Confirms the standard NZ GST rate is 15%. Used only to normalise explicitly GST-exclusive figures, not to guess whether an unstated source price includes GST.

building-contracts-2026.title: Contracts for your building project
building-contracts-2026.note: Building Performance guidance last updated 15 January 2026. Residential building work costing $30,000 or more including GST requires a written contract; disclosure and checklist requirements also apply at that threshold or when requested.

ranz-comparing-quotes.title: Comparing Quotes
ranz-comparing-quotes.note: RANZ guidance reviewed 20 October 2026. Explains that roofing quotes may differ because of scope, materials, systems and how work will be carried out, so a price difference alone is not a quality conclusion.

tasman-new-roof-2026.title: How Much Does a New Roof Cost in NZ? (2026 Price Guide)
tasman-new-roof-2026.note: Contractor-authored 2026 guide. Publishes a $15,000-$55,000 headline new-roof range and $90-$180/m² long-run steel installed range, with Auckland context. The page is not a national survey and the displayed table does not explicitly state GST treatment, so RoofHub keeps those limitations attached.

solution-reroof-2026.title: Roof Replacement Cost New Zealand
solution-reroof-2026.note: Contractor-authored 2026 reroof cost guide serving Auckland, Hamilton and Wellington. Retained as source-specific market context rather than a national tariff or estimator rate card.

branz-membranes-matter.title: Membranes do matter
branz-membranes-matter.note: BRANZ technical overview reviewed 20 October 2026. Covers torch-on bitumen, butyl/EPDM, liquid-applied, TPO and PVC membrane families and explains low-slope design and consent considerations. Its general fall guidance is not substituted for the requirements of a selected proprietary system.

codehub-rubco-2023.title: Rubco Butyl Membrane Systems - Appraisal 1006 (2023)
codehub-rubco-2023.note: Product-specific BRANZ appraisal surfaced through Building CodeHub. Shows how substrate, roof/deck fall, wind scope and approved-applicator conditions belong to a named membrane system rather than a generic membrane rule.

nuralite-membrane-options.title: Waterproof Membrane Options
nuralite-membrane-options.note: Manufacturer overview reviewed 20 October 2026. Compares single-ply TPO/EPDM/PVC-KEE, multi-layer bituminous and liquid-applied membrane families. Used for system-selection context, not independent performance ranking.

ardex-tpo.title: TPO Roofing Systems
ardex-tpo.note: Manufacturer system page reviewed 20 October 2026. Confirms TPO is supplied as a complete roofing system with membranes and accessories. Product-specific technical literature remains the authority for installation and detailing.

bp-consents-2026.title: Check if you need consents
bp-consents-2026.note: MBIE Building Performance guidance. All NZ building work must comply with the Building Code; some low-risk work is exempt from consent, and owners should confirm uncertain cases with their council or an appropriate professional.

bp-repair-exemption-2026.title: 1.1 General repair, maintenance, and replacement
bp-repair-exemption-2026.note: Schedule 1 guidance for repair and replacement. Comparable replacement in the same position can be exempt, but the exemption has important limits, including work on components that failed Building Code durability requirements.

canibuildit-2026.title: Can I Build It? consent checker
canibuildit-2026.note: Government decision-support tool based on Schedule 1 exemptions. Useful as a starting point for homeowners; uncertain or unusual work still needs confirmation from the relevant council or qualified professional.

bp-rbw-2026.title: Restricted building work
bp-rbw-2026.note: Explains restricted building work and the requirement for appropriately licensed practitioners where residential work is consented and affects primary structure or weathertightness.

bp-choose-practitioner-2026.title: Choosing a building practitioner
bp-choose-practitioner-2026.note: Current NZ guidance on finding, checking and comparing practitioners. Recommends references, multiple detailed quotes, written agreements, appropriate licensing and checking scope rather than headline price alone.

bp-implied-warranties-2026.title: Implied warranties and defects
bp-implied-warranties-2026.note: Explains Building Act implied warranties for residential building work, including their application for up to 10 years and the distinction from a separate manufacturer or contractor warranty.

bp-consumer-rights-2026.title: Protection for homeowners
bp-consumer-rights-2026.note: Homeowner consumer-protection guidance covering the $30,000 including GST contract threshold, disclosure/checklist requirements and documents that contractors must supply when work is completed.

bp-defects-2026.title: Activate your consumer rights
bp-defects-2026.note: Explains the initial 12-month defect repair period and the broader implied-warranty framework. RoofHub uses this for consumer-rights context, not legal advice on an individual dispute.

ranz-choose-roofer-2026.title: Choosing a Roofer
ranz-choose-roofer-2026.note: Current RANZ consumer guidance on researching roofing companies, defining the required work and checking professional information. Industry-association membership is useful context but does not replace statutory licensing where licensing is required.

ranz-maintenance-2026.title: Maintenance Tips
ranz-maintenance-2026.note: RANZ homeowner maintenance guidance covering drainage, signs of deterioration and working-at-height safety. Used as practical industry context alongside product-specific manufacturer requirements.

ranz-reroof-guide-2026.title: RANZ Re-Roofing Guide
ranz-reroof-guide-2026.note: RANZ describes this as an annually updated NZ consumer guide to reroofing materials, systems, terminology, scope and workmanship. Used for project-planning context rather than contractor ranking.

mrm-internal-moisture-2026.title: Code of Practice v26.09: Internal Moisture
mrm-internal-moisture-2026.note: Current MRM Code of Practice section on condensation, moisture sources, ventilation pathways and underlay in metal-roof assemblies. Technical design must still follow the project-specific compliance path and product requirements.

mrm-underlay-2026.title: Code of Practice v26.09: Underlay
mrm-underlay-2026.note: Current MRM guidance describing underlay as temporary moisture absorption/release rather than a substitute drainage plane, and recommending no more than one compliant layer on a profiled-metal reroof except at laps.

mrm-ventilation-2026.title: Code of Practice: Ventilation Pathways
mrm-ventilation-2026.note: MRM guidance on roof-space ventilation pathways, moisture movement and cases where additional ventilation may be needed. Ventilation is a design response to moisture conditions, not a generic cure for every roof problem.

branz-roof-ventilation.title: Roof space ventilation
branz-roof-ventilation.note: BRANZ bulletin explaining that roof-space ventilation in NZ is primarily about moisture management above ceiling insulation and below roof cladding. Retained as technical background alongside the current MRM Code of Practice.

mrm-flashings-2026.title: Code of Practice v26.09: Flashings
mrm-flashings-2026.note: Current MRM flashing guidance. Defines the purpose of flashings and identifies common types including ridge/hip, barge/verge, parapet cappings, apron and valley; penetration flashings are treated separately.

branz-roof-junction-2026.title: Roof junction detail
branz-roof-junction-2026.note: BRANZ worked detail showing why junctions can require multiple interacting flashings. Used to explain complexity, not as a universal detail for every roof or cladding system.

mrm-compatibility-2026.title: Code of Practice v26.09: Material compatibility
mrm-compatibility-2026.note: Current MRM durability guidance on dissimilar metals, contact and runoff. Material combinations must be checked rather than assuming all roof, flashing, gutter and accessory metals are compatible.

mrm-maintenance-2026.title: Code of Practice v26.09: Preventative maintenance
mrm-maintenance-2026.note: Current MRM guidance on preventative maintenance in vulnerable areas, including severe marine micro-environments and unwashed areas. Used alongside the selected product manufacturer warranty and care requirements.

colorsteel-warranty-2026.title: Warranty & maintenance
colorsteel-warranty-2026.note: Current manufacturer guidance linking product suitability, warranty terms and maintenance to environmental exposure. Coastal distance is a guide only; local conditions, design and position can change the applicable category.

codehub-e1as1-2026.title: Acceptable Solution E1/AS1: Surface Water, Amendment 12
codehub-e1as1-2026.note: Current Building CodeHub record for E1/AS1 Amendment 12. Provides one compliance pathway for disposal of surface water, including roof drainage; project design must use the applicable current compliance route and local rainfall information.

branz-roof-drainage-2026.title: Roof drainage design
branz-roof-drainage-2026.note: BRANZ design guidance on internal and external roof drainage, gutter capacity, downpipes, falls, overflows and rainfall intensity. Used for explanatory context, not to size a specific building from a generic rule.

mrm-glossary-domestic-2026.title: Code of Practice v26.09: Domestic cladding terminology
mrm-glossary-domestic-2026.note: Current NZMRM domestic roofing nomenclature showing common terms including ridging, penetrations, underlay, valleys, barges, aprons, roof lights, gutters and downpipes. Used for NZ terminology, not as a complete design specification.

mrm-drainage-terms-2026.title: Code of Practice v26.09: Roof drainage terminology
mrm-drainage-terms-2026.note: Current NZMRM terminology for external gutters/spouting, internal gutters, secret gutters, valleys and related roof-drainage terms.

mrm-penetrations-2026.title: Code of Practice v26.09: Roof penetrations
mrm-penetrations-2026.note: Current NZMRM roof-penetration guidance. Penetration detailing depends on hole size and shape, roof pitch and type, catchment area, position and durability/compatibility requirements.

mrm-penetration-compatibility-2026.title: Code of Practice v26.09: Penetration durability and compatibility
mrm-penetration-compatibility-2026.note: Current NZMRM guidance requiring compatible materials around penetrations and separate drainage of condensate or corrosive discharge rather than discharge onto metal roof cladding.

mrm-overpainting-2026.title: Code of Practice v26.09: Overpainting
mrm-overpainting-2026.note: Current NZMRM generic preparation and overpainting guidance for metal cladding. It stresses correct preparation, compatible primers/coatings and following the coating supplier instructions.

ranz-roof-coating-cop.title: New Zealand Roof Coating Code of Practice
ranz-roof-coating-cop.note: RANZ roof-coating trade guidance. It states that roof coating is not weatherproofing, requires an initial roof-condition assessment, and only extends the life of a suitable existing roof for a limited time.

worksafe-roof-restoration.title: Roof restoration and maintenance
worksafe-roof-restoration.note: WorkSafe guidance for roof restoration and maintenance tasks. It applies the working-at-height control hierarchy and identifies brittle roofing, inspections, cleaning, repairs and coating work as roof-access hazards requiring suitable controls.

worksafe-working-roofs.title: Working on roofs - good practice guidelines
worksafe-working-roofs.note: WorkSafe roof-work guidance covering safe access, fall hazards, brittle roofing, weather and preferred temporary access such as scaffolding or work platforms.

bp-why-contracts-2026.title: Why contracts are valuable
bp-why-contracts-2026.note: MBIE guidance last updated 14 May 2026. A written contract is mandatory for residential building work costing $30,000 or more including GST; written contracts are recommended below that threshold too.

bp-implied-contract-terms-2026.title: Implied contract terms
bp-implied-contract-terms-2026.note: MBIE guidance on default residential building contract terms, including payments, variations, consents, subcontractors and disputes where a contract is missing required provisions.

branz-roof-moisture-2024.title: Roof space moisture – it’s complicated - Build 202 (2024)
branz-roof-moisture-2024.note: BRANZ discussion of roof-space moisture sources and controls. It warns that the moisture source is not always the roof and covers warm roofs, cold roofs and ventilation as part of a wider moisture strategy.

bp-active-ventilation-2026.title: Active ventilation
bp-active-ventilation-2026.note: MBIE/Building Performance home-ventilation guidance. It says supply air should come from outdoors rather than a potentially polluted roof space, and specifically warns that roof-sourced systems must not be installed where asbestos roof cladding is present.

bp-solar-exemption-2025.title: Solar panel and boundary setback building consent exemption changes
bp-solar-exemption-2025.note: MBIE announcement of roof-mounted solar consent exemptions taking effect 23 October 2025. Building Code, district-plan and exemption conditions still apply, with structural and weathertightness risks to manage.

bp-solar-notes-2025.title: Notes for solar panel arrays: 14.1 to 14.4
bp-solar-notes-2025.note: Current MBIE guidance for solar-array Schedule 1 exemptions. Roof-mounted arrays under 40 m² and not above high wind have one pathway; larger arrays or higher wind require structural fixing design/review by a Chartered Professional Engineer to use the exemption.

bp-insulation-existing-2025.title: Insulation for existing homes
bp-insulation-existing-2025.note: MBIE existing-home insulation guidance. For ceilings without accessible roof spaces, replacing the roofing or ceiling lining can be a useful opportunity to insulate; moisture and clearance details still need correct design and installation.

tenancy-insulation-2025.title: Insulation standard
tenancy-insulation-2025.note: Healthy Homes insulation guidance, last updated 25 September 2025. Rental-property obligations have specific rules and exemptions; inaccessible roof cavities may need attention when reroofing makes them accessible.

bp-h1-repairs-2025.title: Building work repairs, replacements and alterations – H1 compliance
bp-h1-repairs-2025.note: MBIE guidance confirmed current in November 2025 on when repairs, replacements and alterations to existing buildings engage H1 energy-efficiency requirements.

icnz-gradual-damage.title: Gradual deterioration and resultant damage
icnz-gradual-damage.note: ICNZ consumer guide dated October 2019 explaining the common distinction between sudden accidental loss and gradual deterioration, and why reasonable care and maintenance can affect insurance outcomes. Individual policy wording controls.

icnz-claims.title: How to Make an Insurance Claim
icnz-claims.note: ICNZ claim guidance recommending prompt contact with the insurer, documenting damage and checking before disposing of damaged items. It also distinguishes sudden events from wear, tear and maintenance issues.

mrm-glossary-definitions-2026.title: Code of Practice v26.09: Glossary definitions
mrm-glossary-definitions-2026.note: Current NZMRM glossary definitions for common roofing terms including fascia board, eaves, soffit, purlin and rafter. Used for terminology rather than project-specific design.

pmr-repair-restore-2026.title: Re-roof vs roof restoration
pmr-repair-restore-2026.note: Waikato roofing contractor comparison of restoration and reroofing. Useful for practitioner decision signals such as localised repairability versus widespread rust/failing sheets. Commercial service source; RoofHub does not treat its recommendation as independent technical proof.

rrs-repair-restore-reroof-2026.title: Repair, restore or reroof?
rrs-repair-restore-reroof-2026.note: Auckland contractor site showing repair, restoration and reroof pathways plus project examples. The business states it was established in 2014 and has completed 500+ Auckland roofs. Commercial source; individual project accounts are treated as practitioner observations, not general rules.

rrs-decramastic-torbay-2026.title: Decramastic tile to COLORSTEEL  -  Torbay case study
rrs-decramastic-torbay-2026.note: Project-specific Auckland account describing a 1970s Decramastic roof with widespread stone-chip loss, rust-through and multiple leaks before full replacement. Publisher-reported project; not an independent inspection.

rrs-reroof-service-2026.title: Reroofing services and recent reroof projects
rrs-reroof-service-2026.note: Auckland contractor page with recent reroof examples and its stated repair/restoration/replacement distinctions. Commercial source; useful for field patterns and opening-up scope, not for universal lifespan claims.

willymarsh-restoration-2026.title: Roof restorations and re-coating
willymarsh-restoration-2026.note: Auckland roofing contractor with stated 25+ years of hands-on experience. Describes restoration as appropriate only where the roof system remains suitable, with tile/ridge/flashing repairs completed before recoating. Commercial source.

topline-mteden-reroof-2026.title: Mt Eden bungalow reroof  -  hidden timber failure
topline-mteden-reroof-2026.note: Project-specific reroof account for an approximately 160 m² bungalow where significant purlin deterioration became visible after strip-off and about 35 linear metres of purlins were reported replaced. Publisher-reported project.

eh-reroof-hidden-2026.title: RANZ Re-Roofing Guide 2025: What NZ homeowners need to know
eh-reroof-hidden-2026.note: Long-established NZ roofing/maintenance business summarising practical reroof issues including concealed timber, underlay, flashing and moisture problems exposed after removal. The underlying RANZ guide remains the stronger industry authority; this source contributes practitioner framing.

cowperthwaite-tile-restoration-2026.title: Full concrete tile roof restoration project
cowperthwaite-tile-restoration-2026.note: Project-specific Auckland restoration account for a 25-year-old Monier concrete tile roof describing replacement of cracked tiles, cleaning, repointing, sealing and coating. Commercial restoration source; outcome is publisher-reported.

hdk-kumeu-reroof-2026.title: Long run reroof in Kumeu
hdk-kumeu-reroof-2026.note: Project-specific reroof account involving three roof sections of different ages and timber deterioration discovered during removal. Useful for opening-up uncertainty; publisher-reported and commercially interested.

homesmart-concrete-tile-2026.title: Concrete tile roof repairs and restoration
homesmart-concrete-tile-2026.note: Auckland practitioner guide describing local tile replacement, ridge/hip pointing and broader restoration as alternatives to full replacement where damage is not widespread. Commercial service source.

homesmart-metal-roof-2026.title: Corrugated iron and long-run roof repairs and painting
homesmart-metal-roof-2026.note: Practitioner guide describing individual panel replacement, fixing checks, rust treatment, ridge/flashing/valley repair and restoration before considering complete replacement. Commercial service source.

advance-repair-replace-2026.title: Roof repairs or full roof replacement?
advance-repair-replace-2026.note: Auckland roofing business stating it has operated since 1998. It distinguishes local repairable defects from broader replacement cases, but also specialises in replacement, so RoofHub treats replacement recommendations as commercially interested practitioner evidence rather than neutral proof.

roofprotect-iron-2026.title: Iron and corrugated roof repairs and repainting
roofprotect-iron-2026.note: Wellington practitioner guidance stating localised minor rust, loose fixings and worn coating may be repair/recoat candidates where the structure remains reasonable. Commercial restoration/repair source.

dimond-dp955-2026.title: DP955 roofing profile
dimond-dp955-2026.note: Manufacturer technical data for DP955 including 955 mm nominal cover and a 3° minimum pitch, plus material thickness and detailing notes. Applies to this specific profile and must be read with the full manufacturer literature.

gerard-antica-2026.title: Antica steel roofing tile
gerard-antica-2026.note: Manufacturer product specifications for Antica, including nominal dimensions, effective cover, weight and a stated 12° minimum roof pitch. Product-specific, not a rule for all pressed metal tiles.

nuralite-tpo-2026.title: Nuraply TPO
nuralite-tpo-2026.note: Manufacturer guidance for Nuraply TPO including a minimum fall of 1:80 and steeper recommended falls for plywood and concrete/metal substrates. Product/system-specific; full CodeMark and installation requirements control.

viking-fit-purpose-2026.title: Fit-for-purpose membrane roof systems
viking-fit-purpose-2026.note: Manufacturer overview separating low-slope membrane systems by roof build-up and use, including cold, insulated/warm and retrofit contexts. Useful for system-selection questions; not independent comparative testing.

viking-torchon-2026.title: Torch-On bituminous membrane systems
viking-torchon-2026.note: Manufacturer technical overview of Viking Torch-On systems, system variants, approved-applicator requirement and stated appraisal/CodeMark information. Product-specific commercial source.

branz-tile-repair-guide-2026.title: Good Repair Guide: Clay and concrete roof tiles
branz-tile-repair-guide-2026.note: BRANZ repair-guide catalogue page states the guide focuses on repair options for isolated clay and concrete tile roof concerns, while noting the publication should be read with current Code requirements and standards. The full guide is paid content; RoofHub does not reproduce it.

abovefocus-decramastic-leak-2026.title: Decramastic tile roof leak identification and repair
abovefocus-decramastic-leak-2026.note: Wellington contractor project page reporting a persistent Decramastic roof leak that previous repair attempts had not resolved. The page shows water at the building paper and replacement tiles and reports the leak was resolved. RoofHub uses it as a project-specific example that an older textured-metal-tile roof can sometimes receive a local repair; it does not establish asbestos status or prove that local repair is suitable for another roof.

roofrestore-torbay-tile-2026.title: Concrete Tile Roof Restoration, Torbay
roofrestore-torbay-tile-2026.note: Auckland restoration contractor case study reporting an older concrete-tile roof whose substrate was considered structurally sound, with cracked tiles, apron-flashing work and ridge/hip pointing addressed before recoating. RoofHub uses the condition-and-scope sequence as practitioner evidence, but does not adopt the provider-specific life-extension, price-comparison, coating-performance or warranty claims as general facts.
